long_biography.plain_text:
Alessandro Del Bono guided Mediolanum Farmaceutici through an expansion that changed the scale of the pharmaceutical business established by his father, Rinaldo. Under his leadership, the group created a herbal-products subsidiary and acquired Istituto Gentili and Neopharmed from Merck. The two acquired businesses were combined into Neopharmed Gentili, a medicines company with a strong presence in cardiovascular and neurological treatments.

The group separated part of its pharmaceutical portfolio and brought private-equity partners into Neopharmed Gentili. Del Bono remained a senior leader of the affiliate while the family kept a significant investment. He continued to run Mediolanum, which retained its oncology and rare-disease activities.
long_biography.html:
Alessandro Del Bono guided Mediolanum Farmaceutici through an expansion that changed the scale of the pharmaceutical business established by his father, Rinaldo. Under his leadership, the group created a herbal-products subsidiary and acquired Istituto Gentili and Neopharmed from Merck. The two acquired businesses were combined into Neopharmed Gentili, a medicines company with a strong presence in cardiovascular and neurological treatments.

The group separated part of its pharmaceutical portfolio and brought private-equity partners into Neopharmed Gentili. Del Bono remained a senior leader of the affiliate while the family kept a significant investment. He continued to run Mediolanum, which retained its oncology and rare-disease activities.
